rule: Every createAdminClient() call in src/ is trusted with every shelter, so each is either needs-shelter-filter (tenant data a Lanna admin or another shelter must not reach) or cross-shelter with its reason. unclassified names a site that cannot be decided from the code; the check tolerates and lists it. scripts/check-service-role-sites.mjs fails on any call not recorded here. Part 7 of #ykefa, item #ps6ms; docs/decisions/2026-11-17-service-role-sites-audit.md. SCOPE (#srreg, 2026-11-18): the `scope` block below states which of the four ways this system writes with elevated rights are recorded here and which are not; the check fails if it is missing.

src.why: Every createAdminClient() call in src/ is a record in `sites`, with a classification and a reason.

worker.why: Every function in worker/ that reads env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is a record in `workerSites` (the Worker reaches the database over REST, not through createAdminClient). Nine functions in five files on 2026-11-18. hard-coded-security-registry.json's serviceRoleSites names the same five files at file level; this is the per-function record.

scripts.why: 46 files under scripts/ read SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY on 2026-11-18 (check-*, prove-*, dev-signin, deploy, worktree, bootstrap-admin). They run from a person's machine or CI against the DEV project with keys from .env.local, never in a request, never in production's request path. Not recorded one by one: the cost is 46 records that would rot, for no access the shelter's users can reach. Scripts that write through the service role must send the shelter header (scriptShelterHeaders; scripts/check-null-shelter-id.mjs proves no null-shelter row). Brought in later only if a script is ever scheduled against production.

database.why: 91 security-definer or trigger functions write tables and 3 pg_cron jobs run on 2026-11-18 (dev, read by scripts/check-scheduled-writers.mjs --env test, which judges bodies by pattern and prints 12 that send no shelter). A registry here cannot see them; that script is the instrument for this class and `--strict` is its gate. Recording them here would duplicate a live read that already enumerates them, and would go stale at every migration.

sites.reason: Inserts one row into shelter_enquiries, which is installation-level (no shelter_id, 0427): a stranger asks to use the app for a shelter that does not exist yet, so there is no shelter to filter by. Reads nothing back, grants nothing, answers every outcome alike.

workerSites.reason: Reads the user_roles rows (archived_at is null) of its OWN signed-in machine login with the service key, only to learn which shelter(s) to name in x-shelter-id; every proposal after that is made AS that login (so it still needs the Propose a Thai label card) and carries one shelter's header, one shelter at a time. The read is cross-shelter by construction (a headerless read by the login itself sees nothing, which was the fault, #lblcr). docs/decisions/2026-11-18-scheduled-writer-visibility.md.

Cross-shelter because the job is the installation's, not a shelter's.

Reads the key only to compare it, in constant time, with the bearer token a release-mail request carries; it queries nothing and writes nothing.
